Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot timeline — deterministic routing + audit export (Elara SOW attached)

Thanks for the flag, Stephanie. Quick clarifying questions before I scope:

1) "Deterministic routing": do they mean 1:1 sticky routing for a session (affinity) or deterministic hash-based mapping that guarantees the same backend assignment across restarts? The engineering delta differs materially.
2) Pilot traffic profile in the test plan looks light (avg qps 2–5 with burst to 25). Is that accurate?
3) For audit export: do they require both real-time stream + daily batch, or is daily batch acceptable for initial pilot?

Two implementation options we should consider:
- Option A (fast): Reserved/pinned capacity per-tenant + affinity configuration (workload routed to a pinned pool). Estimated scope: 2-week engineering spike + 1–2 week hardening. Lower infra effort, requires dedicated pool (cost uplift).
- Option B (full): Deterministic routing at the runtime layer (stronger guarantee). Estimated scope: 6–8 weeks, more infra and QA.

From a roadmap perspective, Option A can be delivered quickly as a pilot shim with a clear tradeoff (cost vs guarantees). If we commit to Option B, we need to book a roadmap slot and re-evaluate other planned enterprise work.

Can Engineering confirm if Option A meets the "pilot acceptance" needs and provide an ETA & risk/rollback plan? Also include a cost estimate for pinned capacity.

Happy to join a 30-min sync with Elara once we have estimates.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot timeline — deterministic routing + audit export (Elara SOW attached)

Quick tech note from infra/serving: we currently support session affinity (sticky sessions) which covers a large subset of their asks, but not the stronger "deterministic mapping across restarts" they referred to. Key constraints: autoscaling, preemptible instances, and kernel-level placement decisions mean we don't have a global mapping guarantee today.

Feasible path for a fast pilot (Option A variant):
- Create a small dedicated capacity pool (1–2 GPU nodes) pinned to Elara for the pilot window.
- Implement lightweight KV prefetch and warm-cache policy for their prefix to reduce tail variance.
- Hook a scheduled job to export audit logs to S3 (daily) and add a streaming flag for real-time webhook if they want it.

Estimate:
- Spike + config + test harness: ~10 engineering days (2 engineers) => spike ready in ~3 weeks (Nov 8 target for pilot-ready with dedicated pool).
- Production-grade rollout (full deterministic routing): 6–8 weeks, requires infra changes and additional QA.

Temporary workaround cost (pilot): dedicated small pool + storage + networking: estimated additional run-rate ~$9k–$12k/month (ballpark). See attached: dedicated-pool-costs.csv.

Risk/rollback: if pinned pool overloaded, we can fall back to shared pool with affinity and throttle. We'll instrument trace IDs and tenant metrics for the pilot.

If Product is comfortable with Nov 8 pilot-ready ETA and daily export for acceptance, we can commit to the spike this week. Otherwise, full deterministic work will push past their procurement deadline.

— Aditya Rao
Eng Manager, Serving Systems
aditya_rao@redwood.com
